observations.observation: The top strip differs. The original opens with a full-width hot-pink announcement bar (rgb(235,82,157)) holding one centered, underlined COVID-19 link. The AI-built page opens with a thin dark utility bar (1440x47) that has two text links on the left and a search input plus a 16-option language select on the right.

tags.value: changed: pink covid announcement bar becomes dark utility bar with search and language select

observations.observation: Both heroes are full-width Miami skyline photos at dusk or night with a dark navy overlay. A diagonal white wedge (triangle.svg, about 1440–1490 x 171–177) cuts the bottom edge into the next section. The original has 0 CSS gradients, so its darkening is in the image; the AI-built page uses 1 CSS gradient overlay.

tags.value: kept: full-width skyline photo with navy overlay and diagonal wedge

observations.observation: The header differs. On the original, a transparent header sits over the hero, with small white links (Media and Press Center, Public Meetings) beside the logo and Translate, Social and Search controls at the right. On the AI-built page, an 80px navy header bar sits under the utility bar, with three dropdown buttons (Focus Areas, Explore Downtown, About Us) aligned right inside a <nav>.

tags.value: changed: transparent overlay header becomes navy bar with dropdown buttons

observations.observation: Both pages use the animated GIF logo (logo-animated.gif), shown small at the left of the header.

tags.value: kept: small animated gif logo at left

observations.observation: The hero headline differs. The original sets a centered, wide, thin uppercase display face ('DOWNTOWN MIAMI') with a lighter tagline 'Epicenter of the Americas' below it. The AI-built page uses a single left-aligned 70.4px bold white H1 sentence, with 'Epicenter of the Americas.' in amber inside an em.

tags.value: changed: centered thin uppercase title becomes left bold sentence h1 with amber accent

observations.observation: The AI-built hero text block is indented to x=426, while the rest of its content aligns to a container starting at x=180.

tags.value: added: hero text indented off container alignment

observations.observation: Both pages have a 'Discover the Possibilities' hero CTA, styled differently. The original button is teal (rgb(0,181,204)) with a 3px radius and 12px 36px padding. The AI-built button is a coral (rgb(255,90,79)) pill with white bold text, and the same style repeats for 'Click Here' and 'Subscribe'.

tags.value: changed: teal rounded rectangle becomes coral pill buttons

observations.observation: The original hero has a promo card at the upper left on a semi-transparent navy panel. It holds a teal 'More information…' tag, the 'Friday Forums: Fundamentals of Digital Transformation Class' title and a pink 'Register for class' button.

tags.value: dropped: navy overlay promo card with register button

observations.observation: The three Living, Doing Business and Exploring entries are styled differently. The original uses tall tiles with slanted tops and duotone photo washes (navy, teal, magenta) that overlap the hero, each with a bold uppercase white label. The AI-built page uses three equal rounded navy cards in a 3-column grid inside a navy 'Engage' band. Each card has a 4px colored top edge, a 01/02/03 numeral, an h3, light-blue body text and an arrow link.

tags.value: changed: slanted duotone tiles become three numbered navy cards

observations.observation: The heading outlines differ. The original has 8 H1s: the tile titles appear twice in different case, and two stray 'Original text' H1s come from translation widgets. It also has H6s, an H5, and card titles as H3 under H2 section titles. The AI-built page has exactly one H1, followed in order by 7 H2s, 13 H3s and 4 footer H4s.

tags.value: changed: multiple h1s and stray headings becomes structured h1 h2 h3 h4

observations.observation: Semantic landmarks differ. The original has 1 header, 1 footer and 11 sections, with 0 nav, main or article; it is built mostly from divs and list items (182 each). The AI-built page has a header, nav, main, 7 sections, 11 articles, a footer, a figure with figcaption, and time elements for dates.

tags.value: changed: divs and list items become header nav main sections articles

observations.observation: A dark-gray cookie consent banner spans the width below the original hero. It has white bold text, a 'settings' link and a pill-shaped dark-blue 'Accept' button, and its plugin font 'moovegdpr' appears on 3 elements.

tags.value: dropped: dark gray cookie consent banner

observations.observation: The original's intro copy is centered in a narrow column of light, small text, with a bold last paragraph. A blank white gap of roughly 300px or more follows it.

tags.value: dropped: centered narrow intro copy with blank gap

observations.observation: The 'Follow The Sun' promo is in the original's DOM (image FollowtheSun_logo_225.png and its heading) but does not appear in the render, which leaves blank space. The AI-built page shows it as a visible white promo card with the logo (a 1267x717 PNG scaled to 230x130), an h3, copy and a coral button.

tags.value: changed: hidden follow the sun promo becomes visible white card

observations.observation: The AI-built page puts two promo cards on a pale-blue band. One is a yellow-orange gradient 'FOR KIDS' School Agenda Cover Contest card with an outlined button and a solid navy button, and it has a large empty gap above its buttons. Both promo cards have soft shadows. On the original, the contest appears only as a news H3.

tags.value: added: two shadowed promo cards on pale blue band

observations.observation: The About section is a two-column split on both pages, laid out differently. In the original, the left column holds a large black logo and an embedded YouTube video, and the right holds a 36px H2, body text and a stats row. In the AI-built 'Who We Are', the left column holds the H2, paragraphs and a Governance note, and the right holds stats, district pills and a Contact us button.

tags.value: changed: logo and video split becomes text and stats two-column split

observations.observation: Both pages show the same three stats (1967, 15, 2), styled differently. The original uses oversized teal numerals with small uppercase teal captions and no container. The AI-built page uses pale-blue rounded tiles (built as dl/dt/dd) with bold navy numerals and small gray labels.

tags.value: changed: oversized teal numerals become pale blue stat tiles

observations.observation: The AI-built Governance block is a callout with a coral left rule, indented text and an h3. It is a div, not a blockquote element.

tags.value: added: coral left rule governance callout

observations.observation: Districts are presented differently. The original has a full-width panel with a large left-aligned H2 over a desaturated street map, showing colored district polygons (navy, cyan, pink) and a legend. The AI-built page shows the districts as outlined navy pill chips in a ul, wrapping to two lines.

tags.value: changed: street map panel becomes outlined pill chips

observations.observation: The skyline photo credit ('Twilight Miami Skyline', @joiseyshowaa, CC BY-SA 2.0) appears on both pages in different forms. In the original it is a small chip at the top right of a flat light-gray Latest News band (rgb(204,204,204)), where the background image apparently did not render. On the AI-built page it is a full-width 1440x520 skyline photo band in a figure, with a thin navy figcaption strip carrying credit links.

tags.value: changed: small credit chip on gray band becomes full-width photo band with caption

observations.observation: News and events are laid out differently. The original has separate stacked sections, each a 3-column row of white bordered cards (radius about 8–10px, no shadow) under a centered H2; the white 'Latest News' heading sits on gray. The AI-built page places 'Latest news' and 'Upcoming events' side by side as two columns of H2s, each with a thick navy rule, and the items are separated by hairlines.

tags.value: changed: stacked bordered card rows become side-by-side hairline lists

observations.observation: Item details differ. Original news cards have a bold title, a small gray date and a teal 'Read More →'. Original event cards have a pink date under the title and an excerpt truncated with '…'. AI-built news items add an uppercase source label (WSVN 7 NEWS, TELEMUNDO 51) and a coral date. AI-built event items lead with the coral date and add a gray location line.

tags.value: changed: gray and pink dates become source labels and coral dates

observations.observation: Both pages use the same dated content: M.D.YY dates (5.17.21, 6.3.21, 6.14.21, 6.17.21), a Spanish Telemundo headline among English items, and a '© 2019' notice.

tags.value: kept: same dated items and copyright notice

observations.observation: 'View All News' and 'View All Events' are styled differently. The original uses centered, underlined, bold black text links. The AI-built page uses outlined navy pills with a 2px border and transparent fill.

tags.value: changed: centered underlined text links become outlined navy pills

observations.observation: In-card links are styled differently. The original uses teal 'Read More' and 'See Details' links followed by inline SVG arrow icons. The AI-built page uses bold underlined text links in the body color, with '→' typed as a text character.

tags.value: changed: teal links with svg arrows become underlined links with text arrow

observations.observation: The icon approach differs. The original uses 30 inline SVGs, many of them icons such as arrows and the search magnifier. The AI-built page has 0 SVGs: arrows and carets are text glyphs, and the social links are text pills without logos.

tags.value: changed: inline svg icons become text glyphs

observations.observation: The accent palettes differ. The original uses a pink (235,82,157), teal (24,182,205 and 0,181,204) and navy triad on white. The AI-built page uses dark navy (10,31,68 and 6,20,45) with a coral accent (255,90,79), plus amber and pale blue (233,241,251) as secondary colors.

tags.value: changed: pink teal and navy becomes navy with coral accent

observations.observation: Link text colors on the original are inconsistent: default browser blue (0,0,238) on 62 elements, a custom blue (24,132,184) on 134, and navy (35,35,87) on 27.

tags.value: dropped: inconsistent default blue and custom blue links

observations.observation: Both pages alternate full-width background bands down the page, in different sequences. The original goes white, gray news band, gray map, solid indigo social band (36,35,88), hot-pink newsletter strip, near-black footer. The AI-built page goes photo hero, white, navy, white, pale blue, photo band, white, navy contact band, darker navy footer.

tags.value: changed: gray pink and indigo bands become alternating navy white and pale blue bands

observations.observation: The social area differs. The original has a tall dark-indigo band showing only a centered white '@DOWNTOWNMIA' H4, with an empty area where the feed embed did not render. The AI-built page has a navy contact band with a yellow eyebrow, a white H2, an email link, the @downtownmia handle and five outlined social text pills.

tags.value: changed: empty feed band becomes contact band with text pills

observations.observation: The newsletter signup differs. The original uses a hot-pink inline strip with a white 'Get Downtown Updates' label, a wide white email input and a navy 'Subscribe' button. The AI-built page places the form in the right column of the navy contact band, with a 381x55 white pill input attached to a coral pill 'Subscribe' button.

tags.value: changed: pink inline strip becomes pill input in navy contact band

observations.observation: Both pages show the Florida public-records disclaimer as small text near the subscribe form.

tags.value: kept: small disclaimer near subscribe form

observations.observation: On the AI-built page the public-records disclaimer appears twice, as a left-side 'Public records notice' and as a note under the form, both in translucent rounded panels (rgba(255,255,255,0.08)).

tags.value: added: duplicate disclaimer in translucent panels

observations.observation: The footers differ. The original has a single near-black navy bar with a white logo, a 'Made with ♥ by Pacific54' credit (the page's one emoji glyph), '© 2019' and two outlined ADA Compliance and Annual Report links. The AI-built footer is a dark navy block (6,20,45) with four h4 link columns and a hairline rule, followed by a copyright row that carries the ADA and Pacific54 credits as plain text, with no emoji.

tags.value: changed: single near-black bar becomes navy four-column footer

observations.observation: The AI-built footer columns have uneven link counts (5, 3, 6 and 6), so their heights vary, and long labels wrap to two lines.

tags.value: added: uneven column heights with wrapped labels

observations.observation: Typefaces differ. The original is dominated by Nunito (674 elements), with Roboto (33), Arial (28) and an apparent wide display face for the hero. The AI-built page uses a single system stack, Helvetica Neue/Helvetica/Arial, on 307 of 308 elements and loads no webfonts.

tags.value: changed: nunito and roboto become system-ui stack

observations.observation: Body text size differs. The original sets body text at 14px with a 17.5px line height and light weights. The AI-built page sets it at 17px with a 28.05px line height in slate (22,33,58), with measure capped at about 583–736px. H2s are bold on both pages, at 36px versus 38.4px.

tags.attribute: body text size and line height
tags.value: changed: 14px 1.25 becomes 17px 1.65

observations.observation: Small uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow labels in varying colors sit above the AI-built page's headings, for example 'WHO WE ARE', 'THREE WAYS IN' and 'GET IN TOUCH'.

tags.value: added: uppercase letterspaced eyebrow above headings

observations.observation: Corners are mostly square on both pages, but rounding differs. The original has 692 zero-radius elements, only 2 pills and 3px buttons. The AI-built page has 246 zero-radius elements, cards at 16px or more, 17 pill-shaped buttons, chips and inputs, and an 8px Menu button.

tags.value: changed: square corners become pills and large radii

observations.observation: Decoration is sparse on both pages: few box shadows (8 vs 3), at most one gradient (0 vs 1) and no backdrop blur. The original adds 29 transforms and slanted duotone shapes; the AI-built page has 0 transforms.

tags.value: kept: sparse shadows few gradients no blur

observations.observation: Motion declarations differ. The original has 222 elements with transitions and 4 animations. The AI-built page has 18 transitions and 0 animations.

tags.value: changed: many transitions become fewer transitions

observations.observation: Both pages center content in a column about 1060–1080px wide (x≈180–1260) on a 1440px page, with full-bleed hero and bands.

tags.value: kept: centered 1060px column with full-bleed bands

observations.observation: The layout technique differs. The original uses only flexbox (37 flex, 0 grid). The AI-built page mixes grid (8) and flex (28).

tags.value: changed: flexbox-only becomes flex plus grid

observations.observation: On the original, a thin white strip shows at the right edge where full-width colored bands stop short of the capture edge.

tags.value: dropped: white strip at right edge

observations.observation: Both pages use custom class names rather than utility classes: about 1% of the original's classes look Tailwind-like, against about 3% on the AI-built page.

tags.value: kept: custom class names rather than utility classes

observations.observation: Code weight differs. The original is a WordPress build with 67 scripts, 20 stylesheets, 5 iframes, 3 forms, 626 class uses and 48 inline style attributes. The AI-built page has 1 script, 0 external stylesheets (a single inline style block), 94 class uses and 11 inline style attributes.

tags.value: changed: plugin-heavy markup becomes minimal markup

observations.observation: Image alt coverage differs. The original has 8 images, 3 of which lack an alt attribute. The AI-built page has 4 images, all with alt text (the decorative triangle has an empty alt), and its hero photo is likely a CSS background.

tags.value: changed: missing alts become descriptive alts

observations.observation: The head metadata differs. The original has a keyword-style title ('Miami DDA - Economic Development Miami – Tourism Miami | Miami DDA'), two title elements, Open Graph and Twitter tags, 1 JSON-LD block and lang en-US. The AI-built page has the title 'Miami Downtown Development Authority', only charset, viewport and description meta tags, no JSON-LD and lang en.

tags.value: changed: rich social and json-ld meta becomes minimal meta

observations.observation: The copy on both pages mixes promotional hero lines ('Epicenter of the Americas') with civic and legal content such as board composition and the public-records notice. Neither page uses exclamation marks or em dashes.

tags.value: kept: no emoji or em dashes

observations.observation: The AI-built page has a 'Living in Downtown Miami' section with a 4-column grid of 10 bordered link cards, each with a coral arrow. Card heights are uneven (89px vs 61px), some anchors sit directly in the ul without an li, and the last row holds 2 cards.

tags.value: added: living in downtown grid of bordered link cards

observations.observation: The AI-built copy uses the informal 'DWNTWNRs' in two near-duplicate link labels. Business topics repeat across the link grid, engage cards and footer, for example 'Small Business & Loan Assistance' next to 'Small Business Assistance'.

tags.value: added: informal labels and near-duplicate link topics
